 Order
This first application under Section 483 of BNSS has been filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

2. The applicant has been arrested on 20.01.2025 in connection with Crime No.427/2023 registered at Police Station Mungawali, District Ashoknagar for the offences punishable under Sections 363,
366-A, 376(2)
(n), 376(3), 467, 468, 471 of IPC and Section 3/4, 5L/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false averments, applicant has been taken into custody, who is in custody since 20.01.2025.

He submits that in the statement recorded under Section 161 of CrPC, prosecutrix as well as her parents did not say anything against the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5651 2 MCRC-5680-2025 applicant.

He submits that previously W.P. No.35453/2024 (Habeas Corpus) was filed, in which State Counsel submitted status report containing the fact that the prosecutrix or her mother has stated that no offence has been committed by the applicant and when the prosecutrix was sent for medical examination, her parents Govind Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34811463/
1 said that they do not want to examine the prosecutrix medically and admittedly, no medical examination has been done.

entities.text: Govind Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With these submissions, he submits that the applicant has been implicated falsely and prays for grant of bail.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent No. 1/State submits that although previously the prosecutrix and her parents stated that the applicant has not committed any offence and they refused to medically examine the prosecutrix, but later on, in the statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, the prosecutrix has stated clearly against the applicant, therefore, he cannot be granted benefit of bail.
5.
Learned counsel appearing for the complainant/respondent No. 2 has also supported the versions of learned counsel for the State.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary available on record.
7.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments made by learned counsel for both the parties, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5651 3 MCRC-5680-2025 with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court as and when required.
He shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of CrPC/482(3) of BNSS.

(DWARKA DHISH BANSAL) JUDGE Abhi Govind Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34811463/
